articles.title: How Alex Eala's Wimbledon Stunner Is a Victory for Every Underdog
articles.summary: In a stunning Wimbledon upset, 21-year-old Alex Eala defeated defending champion Iga Swiatek to become the first Filipino to reach a Grand Slam fourth round. She dedicated the win to her younger self and "all the girls with ruffled socks and chubby cheeks," capturing hearts worldwide.

articles.title: The Accidental Invention of the Teenager—and How They've Been Running Pop Culture Ever Since
articles.summary: The U.S. accidentally created the teenager in the mid-20th century, and they've been reshaping society ever since. From rock 'n' roll and drive-ins to Walkmans and beepers, each generation's obsessions—music, fashion, hangouts—became cultural landmarks that still influence us today.

articles.title: How Irish Immigrants Became the Backbone of the Continental Army
articles.summary: Up to 50% of the Continental Army was of Irish heritage—immigrants who fled British oppression and brought a deep grudge to the American Revolution. John Barry, an Irish-born captain, became the "father of the U.S. Navy" after capturing British ships and safeguarding gold for the new nation.
